html:
The Pskov Republic was a city-state in northwest Russia, centred on the town of Pskov on the Velikaya river, from 1348 to 1510. It is on the map for 1492 and 1500.

Pskov had long been a junior partner of Novgorod, and in 1348 Novgorod accepted its independence. Like Novgorod it was run by a town assembly, the veche, which met in the stone citadel, the Krom, and chose its princes and officials. Its merchants traded with the Hanseatic towns, and its walls faced the Livonian Order just to the west, with which it fought many border wars.

As Moscow grew, Pskov leaned on it for protection against Livonia and Lithuania. In 1510 Vasili III annexed it outright, took down the veche bell, and moved hundreds of leading families to Moscow. It was the last of the old Russian city republics to fall.
